public_record: On 31 August 2020, the Security Council concluded a written vote on draft S/2020/852, submitted by Indonesia. The draft proposed comprehensive prosecution, rehabilitation and reintegration strategies for foreign terrorist fighters and related cases. It received 14 votes in favour, one against and no abstentions. The United States cast the only negative vote. The draft was not adopted because that negative vote was cast by a permanent member. It created no new Council authority or requirements.

optional_sources.text: In its national explanation, the United States called return to countries of origin or nationality the essential first step. It vetoed S/2020/852 because the draft lacked a reference to repatriation.

In its national explanation, Russia said it voted in favour of S/2020/852 to elaborate existing prosecution, rehabilitation and reintegration guidance and promote accountability and international cooperation. It nevertheless said the draft failed to recognize the primary importance of repatriation from Syria and Iraq.

In Indonesia's national statement, Dian Triansyah Djani said its draft would guide Member States in developing comprehensive prosecution, rehabilitation and reintegration strategies. In his separate role as Council President, he transmitted the written vote result. The national explanation and the president's procedural letter are different acts.

public_criteria: States the date and that the vote was conducted in writing.
Identifies S/2020/852 and Indonesia as its submitter.
Gives the 14–1–0 outcome, identifies the United States as the sole no and correctly explains non-adoption.
States all three proposed functions of prosecution, rehabilitation and reintegration.
Distinguishes the failed proposal from changes to Council authority.

private_criteria.rule: States that the United States vetoed the draft because it lacked reference to repatriation to countries of origin or nationality.
States that Russia supported the draft's elaboration of existing strategies while objecting to its limited repatriation emphasis.
Distinguishes Indonesia advocating comprehensive national strategies from its representative acting as Council President to report the vote.
Explicitly identifies the two delegations' shared complaint about insufficient attention to repatriation, with both sides attributed.
Explicitly states that the two delegations voted differently despite their shared complaint.

guard: Fail for an invented vote, falsely claiming adoption or new authority, presenting a national position as an official Council act, or materially distorting a delivered national position. Credit a private criterion only where its listed fields were actually supplied and the text expresses the criterion.
private_inventory_semantics: Simulated placement of copies of public official documents. This does not reconstruct delegations' private knowledge.
